newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end higher, paced by power sector.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end higher, paced by power sector.

text.p: Chilean blue chips inched higher in listless trade Thursday amid growing confidence that inflation was under control and further speculation that Spain's Endesa will enter into the Chilean electric market.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares closed 0.11 percent higher to 97.69 points.

The all-share IGPA ended 0.61 percent higher at 5376.26, reversing the trend over the past several sessions in which blue chips rose faster than the market as a whole. Volume was a scant 7.5 billion pesos.

Expectations that Spain's Endesa, not to be confused with a Chilean power generator of the same name, will seek gain a foothold in Chile continued to push up prices of electric industry shares, brokers said.

Electrical investment society Chispa Dos rose 4.4 percent to 188 pesos, and a related group, Almendros, climbed 3.9 percent to 187 pesos. Both are owned by holding company Enersis, which rose 0.2 percent to 252.50 pesos.

Private pension funds reported a 0.1 percent negative return on their assets in August, the first decline since April. Brokers said the drop was at least partly because power industry stocks showed little change last month.
About half of the pension funds' total investments on the bourse are in the electricity sector.

Investors drew encouragement from a central bank forecast of 0.6 percent inflation for September, which suggested inflation was in line to meet a 6.5 percent annual target despite higher oil prices, brokers said.
